analysis.title: Macro Multi-Asset Quarterly Q4 2026
key_insights: Deglobalization's secular inflationary forces could force central banks to raise rates for longer than markets currently anticipate.
Sectors and regions starved of capital by the AI boom may attract capital again. Reduced global liquidity is a challenge for speculation but should lead to more rational capital allocation.
Global profits are strong and accelerating broadly. About 75% of super growth stocks (forecast growth above 25%) are outside the US.

International earnings growth is expected to accelerate into 2027 as US growth peaks. Global liquidity is beginning to tighten as central banks contend with ongoing inflation. Sentiment remains moderate outside the US.

The team favors diversification into cheaper assets that may perform better with higher inflation and rates: dividend, value and select cyclical equities, and real assets. International equities are preferred over more expensive US stocks where earnings are peaking.

In fixed income the team is cautious on high-grade corporate bonds given historically tight credit spreads. It emphasizes Treasuries, high-quality floating-rate securities and municipal bonds, with shorter duration than the benchmark.

US trailing earnings growth is around 30% and is expected to slow to the mid-teens in 2027. Much of the slowdown comes from the Magnificent 7, whose consensus growth of above 50% for 2026 falls to in line with the broader market in 2027.
EM and Japan profits are expected to keep accelerating. EM improvement still comes from Taiwan and South Korea (AI infrastructure suppliers) but is broadening across more countries.
Europe is expected to see modest earnings improvement into 2027 with growth still tepid. The growth gap between Europe and the US should narrow markedly in 2027.

Liquidity is tightening across major developed markets as more central banks hike. Further hikes are likely needed to meaningfully slow activity. Real yields are at post-GFC highs and yield curves have flattened since end-2025.
Credit conditions remain unrestrictive. Spreads have risen from recent lows on heavy supply and higher government yields, but banks' willingness to lend has not changed.

US equity leadership is very narrow, concentrated in AI-linked mega caps, leaving markets vulnerable to AI disappointment. A similar concentration in Taiwanese and South Korean tech exists in EM, though valuations there have cheapened.
A near-record number of S&P 500 stocks have negative betas, which the team says allows building a diversified equity portfolio now.

Positioning: favor international over US equities, value over growth within the US, stay wary of duration, find credit spreads unattractive, hold gold as a diversifier, and see FX uncertainty from fiscal risks and rate hikes.

sector_views.rationale: Cheaper assets expected to do better in a higher-inflation, higher-rate environment.
Expected to benefit from higher inflation and rates.
Earnings growth is peaking, valuations are expensive and leadership is crowded.
Spreads are historically tight and unattractive versus risk in other asset classes.

earnings_insights: US trailing EPS growth is around 30% y/y and is forecast by Janus Henderson to slow to the mid-teens in 2027.
Magnificent 7 consensus EPS growth is above 50% for 2026 and is expected to decline to in line with the broader market in 2027.
Europe earnings growth is forecast to improve modestly into 2027 from a tepid level. EM and Japan earnings growth is forecast to keep accelerating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Elevated level expected to peak and decelerate.
Consensus growth expected to fall to market-like levels in 2027.
Real yields weigh on valuations, especially US equities.

macro_indicators.reading: Hiking in US, Europe and Japan; EM on hold
macro_indicators.interpretation: More hikes likely needed to meaningfully slow activity.

risk_factors: Central banks may need to keep raising rates longer than markets expect due to deglobalization-driven inflation.
Narrow AI-driven leadership leaves US equities vulnerable to disappointment in AI investment.
Concentration of EM profits in Taiwan and South Korea technology stocks.
Tight credit spreads and rising bond supply and government yields.
Fiscal risks and rate hikes create FX uncertainty.
Tightening global liquidity may challenge speculative assets.
vol_and_positioning: Equity exposure among investors indicates high bullishness. US sentiment is rated Exuberance while Europe, Japan and EM are Neutral.
Market leadership is very narrow, with near-record numbers of US stocks with negative 3y beta.
Credit spreads have risen from recent lows but remain unattractive versus risk in other asset classes.
geopolitical: Deglobalization's secular inflationary forces are cited as complicating central bank policy.
